mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which lowers discount rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is declining, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 4.5% and remains elevated for two consecutive months, it signals a tightening cycle that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong aggregate demand, which signals robust corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in RSAFS and HOUST fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative coefficient with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a low unemployment regime (UNRATE < 4.0%), a rising labor force (PAYEMS) indicates tight labor market conditions that support corporate profit growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% and PAYEMS is rising, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing activity, which signals stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3.5% and remains above this level for two consecutive months, it signals persistent inflation that may lead to monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.5% for 2 consecutive months, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and a rise in consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a coordinated monetary and fiscal stimulus that boosts equity valuations and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in RSAFS fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a negative coefficient with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In a high industrial production regime (INDPRO > 105.0), a rising industrial output (INDPRO) signals sustained manufacturing strength that supports corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 105.0 and INDPRO is rising, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
